profile.headline: SWE @ Optiver | CS @ Illinois
profile.summary: Hello! My name is Rishi, and I'm a college student studying computer science at UIUC, with particular interest in the areas of machine learning, computer vision, data science, high-performance computing, and quantitative trading.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: I helped develop the back-end framework of a Gies College of Business data hub using Django to gather and organize research data. We leveraged AWS technologies to dynamically pull from various data sources and maintain up-to-date, flexible data to facilitate future research projects. I also contributed to the creation of a website UI to house our data hub using React and Figma to create intuitive and user-friendly front end.

positions.title: Machine Learning Engineer Intern
positions.description: I trained several computer vision models using Darknet and YOLOv3 to identify CAT vehicles and people, with the aim of strengthen safety measures in worksites. To improve the efficacy of CV models, I automated the process of synthetically generating training images using Python and Blender’s Python API, which allowed us to diversify training datasets. I also conducted a study to measure the impact of label variation on model efficacy and mAP scores using Amazon SageMaker and Docker containers, in order to better curate training data for future models.

positions.title: Backend Engineer
positions.description: I helped build a back-end microservices architecture using CRUD operations to maintain the dynamically linked data points and plots processed by Rescon AI. I developed a templated querying system to allow users to easily search through and access research data relevant to them. On the business planning side, I wrote grant proposals for various business venture competitions, helping raise thousands of dollars in funding and resources.

positions.title: CS 126 (Software Design Studio) / CS 128 (Intro to CS II) Course Assistant
positions.description:
I was responsible for conducting code review among a group of 5 students, grading projects, and providing feedback, in order to strengthen student software development techniques, especially focusing on encapsulation, modular design, flexibility, and readability.

I contributed to the development of course infrastructure to improve student outcomes. I helped create supplementary assignments to improve student understanding of complex topics in Java and C++ programming, and helped test new assignments to enhance learning and expose students to new, important computer science applications. I also conducted weekly office hours to help reinforce students' understanding of course content.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description: I developed a chatbot in React to facilitate negotiation between buyers and sellers, which is being franchised to help buyers to find better deals and sellers to increase sales. I organized a team of developers to integrate the chatbot with an AI-based buyer/seller matching algorithm, in order to guide the chatbot dialogue flow. I conducted end-to-end testing of new software to quickly resolve issues and build smoother user experience.

positions.title: Computer Science Instructor
positions.description: I taught computer science concepts and JavaScript/Java programming to 150 elementary/middle school students in the Piscataway/Edison area. I helped prevent the gradual loss of customers hurting the business by overhauling teaching techniques and increasing parent outreach, which led to marked increases in student engagement and customer retention. With the COVID-19 pandemic, I led the implementation of remote learning to sustain student learning and growth.

positions.title: Machine Learning Researcher
positions.description: I trained a convolutional neural network using Jetson Inference and NVIDIA TensorRT to accurately detect humans in the environment through NVIDIA TX-1’s built-in camera. I then integrated this algorithm with an iRobot Create 2 using various Python libaries, in order to simulate a self-driving car with effective safety protocols to reduce traffic injuries. I led a team of 6 researchers in testing the robot’s reliability in avoiding collision with humans in varied environments to show the safety of autonomous vehicles; succeeded in over 50 unique test situations.
